maps.points.underkeep_surroundings.dialo: The forest opens into a quiet glade where the ground has collapsed. A wide pit yawns at its center, roots and stones jutting from the soil.
Large chunks have been bitten away from below, not broken by the fall.
You don't have enough gold. Torren raises an eyebrow.
"A discount doesn't help if you're broke."
Choose “Pay 250 gold.” (You must have at least 250 Gold Coins)
You hand over the coins. Torren nods, pleased, and offers the fragment with a careful, almost ceremonial gesture.
"A wise purchase."
Choose “Pay 300 gold.” (You must have at least 300 Gold Coins)
Choose “Pay 300 gold.” (Fewer than 300 gold coins)
"Come back when you have enough money."
Choose “We don't have the coins right now. We'll return later.”
"If you change your mind, I'll be around the tower for a while."
"Something dug its way up from underneath," you say.
Choose “Pay 250 gold.” (Depends on story progress)
"If fate is kind, our paths will cross again."
"I'll be watching your progress."
With those cryptic words, he walks toward the treeline and disappears into the forest.

The grove lies damp, rain still dripping from the crowns of trees. An old druid leans upon his staff, robes heavy with water, his beard tangled like roots. When you step closer, he straightens, his gaze sharp despite the years.
Event opening (Mounds that have been processed “The Source? ”)
The druid's gaze lingers on you. His pupils darken.
"You carry more than road dust on your hands. The signs... I see them clear now. Guardian fallen. Not by fate, but by your doing."
"Fools. Do you know what you unbind? The wards are chains upon a storm older than this land. Break them... and all of Underkeep drowns in shadow."
The druid raises his staff. Old roots tangle beneath your feet.
Choose “Listen to nature.”
"You have not honored the pact. The forest shall judge you! Awake!"
Event opening (Mounds that have not been processed “The Source? ”)
"You return. I hoped the forest had not turned you aside."
Subsequent dialogue (depending on the progress of the "The Fallen Stone" mission)
"You have walked where the stone has fallen. Tell me, what truth did the earth yield?"
Inform him about the fallen obelisk.
"Tell me, do you come with news, or only with excuses?"
Sorry, we haven't been there yet.
Choose “Sorry, we haven't been there yet.”
"Then hurry! With each passing day the enemy grows stronger and delay only feeds his hand."
You kneel and open yourself to the forest, but it's silent. No birds, no insects, nothing.
Choose “Inform him about the fallen obelisk.”
The druid listens, his staff trembling as you recount how vampiric beetles gnawed beneath the earth until the obelisk sank and shattered.
"The tower was not raised for glory. It was raised to weigh down a hunger that should never walk."
"Yet stone alone is brittle. So its ward was broken into four powers of old, each bearing a fragment of the binding."
He turns away, lost in thought.
"This balance is broken. The seal falters. I must act. Though I fear it may already be too late."
"Do not leave Underkeep. You were brought here for a reason. And now, more than ever, this land needs heroes to stand against the dark."
We have found it This strange book…… Is it useful? (Holding) Ancient Book: The Last Guardian)
What can we do?
Choose “We found this strange book. Is it of any use?”
"Life fled this place," you whisper. "Even the roots keep their distance."
The druid carefully turns a few brittle pages before looking up.
"Extraordinary... These books were written within the tower itself. How one found its way out remains a mystery."
"I have seen only one such volume before."
"It speaks of the ancient guardian who once watched over these woods. I have not seen him for many years... it only confirms what I have feared."
He hands the book back with great care.
Choose “What can we do?”
The druid's gaze sinks into the forest as though he were listening for an answer.
"There is always a way to strike back at the dark. Yet now, the path lies hidden from me."
With a motion both weary and solemn, he presses a small amulet into your hand.
"Take this. A ward for the trials before you. Stand firm, and you will not stand alone."
Before you rises a tall stone monolith, its surface scarred by age yet still traced with runes.
Within moments, his form melts into the high oaks, leaving only the whisper of leaves.
Subsequent dialogue (processed "Source" of the tomb)
Around the fallen stone and along the forest's edge, shapes take form. Dryads wrought of bark and shadow, their eyes burning with old wrath. Deadly guardians of the grove.
The druid's cloak melts into the trees, and in moments he is gone, leaving only the forest's judgment to fall upon you.
Subsequent dialogue (not yet processed "Source" of the tomb)
"Strangers. These stones protect the Tower, and my forefathers guarded them before me. Tell me, what brings you here?"
Dialogue options (task "Wards of the West" is in progress)
We seek only knowledge of these stones and their purpose.
These obelisks... Tell us what they guard.
Our path is our own. We ask no questions of you, nor welcome yours.
The symbols are old, their meaning lost. You cannot read them.
Khelebar sent us to learn about the obelisks.
"We tread where the river carries us. Even stone yields, in time." (Requires Slugman)
"The forest aches. We mean no harm." (Requires Elk)
Select “The forest aches. We mean no harm.” / “The forest aches. I can feel it too. We mean no harm.”
"You hear it as well," druid says quietly. "The roots crying beneath the evil... you're not blind to it."
You nod. "We seek to understand."
He studies you for a moment longer, then lowers his staff. "Then the forest will not bar your way."
Choose “We tread where the river carries us. Even stone yields, in time.”
The druid studies you for a long moment, his expression unreadable.
"A patient soul," he says quietly. "You move as the tide does. The world could learn from that."
Attempt to decipher the runes. (Party member required: Wizard, Available once)
"If you came seeking purpose, perhaps the current brought you for a reason."
Dialogue options (task "Wards of the West" is not currently in progress)
"The forest aches. I can feel it too. We mean no harm." (Requires Elk)
Choose “We seek only knowledge of these stones and their purpose.”
The druid's eyes narrow, his staff tapping once against the wet earth.
"I do not know who sent you or what you seek. Help me, and perhaps I will have reason to trust you."
Choose “These obelisks... Tell us what they guard.”
He stares at you in silence, as though weighing stone against flesh.
Choose “Our path is our own. We ask no questions of you, nor welcome yours.”
The druid inclines his head, a bitter smile tugging at his lips.
Choose “Attempt to decipher the runes.”
"You refuse to explain yourselves, yet expect answers from me? Earn my trust first."
Choose “Khelebar sent us to learn about the obelisks.”
The druid's face hardens, his voice edged with old quarrel.
"Khelebar? That meddling old fool is still sending people into my woods?"
"Our disagreements can wait. For now, I need proof that you can be trusted."
"And should you show the mark of true intent, I will share a small secret with you. One of the ancient obelisks lies hidden in a secret grove, southwest of the Tower."
"Now. While the stones stand, the seal holds. But one of the obelisks has sunk into the earth in the north-western reaches of Underkeep."
His eyes lock on yours, hard as the runes around you.
Select “The forest aches. We mean no harm.” / “The forest aches. I can feel it too. We mean no harm.” (Depends on story progress)
"My watchers have spoken. You've already been there. Good. Now tell me, what befell the fallen stone?"
You trace the weathered runes with your fingers, searching for familiar patterns.
"Find the fallen obelisk and discover what brought it down. I must know whether its power still holds."
"Return with what you learn. Then we can speak."
Choose “Study the lock.” (Depends on story progress)
Before you rises the Underkeep. An ancient tower standing watch over the land long after its builders have vanished.
The main gate stands sealed. Magic, iron and stone wed in an accord.
At its center is an enormous circular lock unlike any you have seen. Its metal shows no sign of rust or wear.
Choose “Insert the first key fragment.” (Depends on story progress)
The final fragment settles into place. The seal completes itself and the Tower is opened.
Choose “Insert the first key fragment.”
Stone grinds against stone as the ancient mechanism awakens.
At the bottom rests a fallen monolith, its runes faint beneath the dirt. The pit is too deep to jump, the walls too soft to climb.
A few symbols almost resemble fragments of ancient magical script, but the similarities end there.
The gate of the Underkeep remains sealed.
Insert the first key fragment. (Possessing the First Runic Segment, can be used only once)
Insert the second key fragment. (Possessing the Second Runic Segment, can be used only once)
Insert the third key fragment. (Possessing the Third Runic Segment, can be used only once)
Insert the fourth key fragment. (Possessing the Fourth Runic Segment, can be used only once)
Study the lock. (Party member required: Thief, Available once)
Choose “Study the lock.”
You inspect the lock for several moments before slowly lowering your hand.
The craftsmanship is beyond anything you have ever encountered. Metal and enchantment are fused so completely that the distinction no longer exists.
"No ordinary tools will open this. The lock and its enchantment are one."
"Too old," you say. "Whatever language this is, it predates anything I know."
You fit the fragment into one of the empty arcs.
It settles without resistance. For a brief moment, the runes around the seal dim... then return to silence.
Choose “Insert the second key fragment.”
The fragment slides into place with a muted click.
A low vibration passes through the gate, felt more in the bones than heard.
Choose “Insert the third key fragment.”
As the fragment locks in, the runes flare faintly, tracing the circle of the seal.
Dust falls from the stone above, disturbed by something shifting behind the gate.
Choose “Insert the fourth key fragment.”
Stone grinds softly as the seal loosens, the ancient lock finally yielding.
Though you cannot understand them, you carefully trace each symbol onto parchment.
Dawn breaks over autumn leaves, yet this side of Underkeep radiates unnatural heat.
A hiss cuts the silence. Dry, patient, close. This place breathes with scales. Snakes.
Use infravision. (Requires Dwarf)
Inspect the tracks. (Requires Slugman)
Sense the animals. (Requires Elk)
Look for traces of magic in the air. (Requires Wizard)
Choose “Inspect the tracks.”
You follow several snake trails through the dust.
The marks are gouged deep into the ground, cutting through roots, even stone.
"Madness," you whisper. "They move like creatures trying to tear the world apart."
You already traced each symbol onto parchment.
Choose “Use infravision.”
You narrow your eyes and let your infravision take over.
The world shifts into shades of heat and stone, but then the sunlight gets in the way.
"Bah. Works better underground."
Choose “Sense the animals.”
You kneel, fingers brushing the damp soil. Beneath it, a pulse. Angry. Territorial. The snakes know you're here.
"Their ground," you whisper. "And they mean to defend it."
Choose “Look for traces of magic in the air.”
You focus, drawing the world into silence. The air itself feels twisted by the ancient magic radiating from the tower.
"Animals near a magic tower rarely stay normal. Keep your distance."
Before you rises a tall stone monolith, its surface scarred by age yet still traced with glowing runes. A silent weight hangs in the air around it.
The path ends at a wall of rough palisades surrounding an Orc camp. Firelight flickers between the sharpened logs.
Guards watch from the shadows with crossbows drawn, ready for trouble.
"Hold up. They're ready for a fight." (Requires Warrior)
"Let me try talking to them." (Requires Thief)
"Check for magical wards." (Requires Wizard)
"Check the collapse." (Requires Dwarf)
Choose “Check for magical wards.”
You study the barricades.
No wards. No enchantments. Just wood, steel, and numbers.
"Magic would be easier."
You loose an arrow toward one of the guards.
The shaft strikes true, then skips harmlessly from a metal breastplate.
The Orc laughs and pounds a fist against his armor.
Choose “Let me try talking to them.”
You step forward with empty hands and a friendly smile.
An arrow lands in the dirt a few steps ahead.
"Listen to nature." (Requires Elk)
A voice from behind the palisade growls something in orcish. It does not sound welcoming.
"Well, I tried."
Choose “Hold up. They're ready for a fight.”
You quickly scan the camp - barricades, watch positions, steel glinting in torchlight. These aren't lazy drunks. They're dug in and waiting.
At least a dozen Orcs. Maybe more.
You crack your knuckles. "Possible. But it won't be easy."
You spot a familiar crimson cloak near the Underkeep Tower. Torren stands beside the path, studying the ancient stonework. He looks up as you approach and offers a slight smile.
"Well, well. We cross paths again. Seems I'm not the only one following old mysteries."
"Back again? Changed your mind, perhaps?"
"The offer still stands. If you're here for the key... we can discuss it."
You kneel near the edge of the pit and study the ground.
What are you doing here?
Choose “What are you doing here?”
"What am I doing here?" He gestures toward the towering structure.
"Same as you, I imagine. Trying to learn what this Tower was built for. I've found a few interesting clues."
Have you found something?
Show him the vial you found earlier. (Possesses Unknown Tincture; can be chosen only once.)
Tell him you used the vial. (Used a dose to deal with the tree people; can only be used once.)
Choose “Show him the vial you found earlier.”
You show him the small green vial you found near the village wall.
Torren blinks, then lets out a soft, amused breath.
No fresh tracks. No deer, not even a rabbit.
"Oh? I dropped this? Truly?"He waves a hand lightly. "No need to return it. Keep it. Perhaps you'll still find a clever use for it out there."
Choose “Tell him you used the vial.”
You mention the vial, how you used it, and what became of the creature in the marsh.
For a brief moment Torren's expression stills entirely, unreadable.
"A curious tale. But I'm afraid that vial wasn't mine. I've never carried anything of the sort."
His voice is calm. Completely calm. Too calm to read anything beneath it.
Choose “Have you found something?”
"Truth be told," he says lightly, "I've found something interesting. A shard of an old key."
He reaches into his cloak and reveals a piece of carved rune-stone. It's shaped like part of a larger key. Without question, it's valuable.
Would you join us and give us the key for opening the tower? (once only)
The collapse itself bears no sign of magic. But in the air, faint threads of power still linger.
What do you want for it? (once only)
"Give us the key. Now." (Requires a Warrior, Available once)
"Do you know what that key opens?" (Party member required: Wizard, Available once)
Choose “Do you know what that key opens?”
Torren glances at the artifact and shrugs.
"Not for certain, but if I had to guess..."
He looks toward the distant tower.
"...I'd say the entrance to Underkeep Tower."
Choose “Would you join us and give us the key for opening the tower?”
Torren raises a brow, surprised by the offer. "Join you? Tempting, in theory."
"This was high magic," you say quietly. "Old, but strong. Someone or something once commanded it."
"But no. The tower gives me... odd chills. I prefer watching its secrets from the outside. Besides, you'd handle what's inside far better than I ever could."
He gestures toward the key fragment. "If you want this for your exploration, we can still discuss a price."
Choose “Give us the key. Now.”
You step forward, making your intent clear. Torren chuckles genuinely amused.
"Bold, but wasted on me. That approach hasn't worked in... well, longer than you'd believe."
"If you want it, I can sell it. But it will not be free. Otherwise, it stays with me."
Choose “What do you want for it?”
"A fair question. Something like this rarely shows itself twice."
"Three hundred gold, and it's yours. A modest price for a piece of something carved so long ago."
Pay 250 gold.
Choose “Check the collapse.”
Pay 300 gold.
We don't have the coins right now. We'll return later.
"Three hundred? That's robbery." (Party member required: Thief, Available once)
Choose “Three hundred? That's robbery.”
You glance at the key, then at Torren.
"Two hundred and fifty."
Torren thinks for a moment.
"You bargain like a merchant and look like a thief."
"Fine. Two hundred and fifty."
Choose “Pay 250 gold.” (Fewer than 250 gold coins)
